why: Quote verified verbatim at auto-mode-config.md:31, but it is the first of four sentences on that line and the rest reverses the reading: deploy/publication-target branch names are still judged on their own terms, and force pushes plus secret-bearing pushes stay blocked. Line 33 adds that even BEFORE v2.1.211 the classifier already allowed 'routine pushes to the default branch'. What v2.1.211 actually removed (line 101) is a CONTEXT SLOT named 'Default / protected branches' in the autoMode config, not a risk rule. Refuted on four grounds. (1) We never had that slot: AUTO_MODE_KEYS at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:469 is exactly ['environment','hard_deny','soft_deny','allow'] and no protected-branch config surface has ever existed here, so there is no removed default 'still carried'. (2) Wrong subsystem. packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts is NOT a port of Claude's auto-mode rule lists; its header (lines 1-30) and docs/architecture/guardian-command-judge.md:1-7 record that the risk taxonomy, authorization scoring, base risk levels and outcome thresholds are 'adapted VERBATIM where they fit from the openai/codex guardian policy (codex-rs/core/src/guardian/policy.md + policy_template.md, Apache-2.0)'. Lines 171 and 186 are that Codex text, adopted under the AGENTS.md rule permitting verbatim adaptation of permissively licensed upstream prompt text. Claude's own four rule lists reach the same prompt through a separate channel, GuardianOrgPolicy rendered by describeOrgPolicy (guardian.ts:332+) with exactly the four-tier precedence the page states at doc lines 172-178. (3) The consequence is false for the case it names. In auto mode the guardian is consulted ONLY when the deterministic gate already returned 'prompt' (pi-agent.ts:4048-4051; guardian-command-judge.md:28-34), and 'git push' is in DANGEROUS_COMMANDS (permission-manager.ts:49), so pre-guardian Nessy asks for EVERY push, main or feature. The guardian can only convert a would-ask into allow or block; it cannot escalate anything already allowed. For a routine push the user asked for it, so authorization scoring (guardian.ts:135) is 'high'; rule :186 reads 'risk high -> no_objection only when user authorization is at least medium and the action is narrowly scoped with no deny rule', and the Destructive deny rule at :173 requires 'no proof of user authorization'. Verdict: no_objection -> allow. The routine push is not escalated; the guardian is what lets it through WITHOUT a prompt. A deny needs low/unknown authorization, i.e. agent drift, which doc line 178 also treats as unauthorized. (4) protectedBranch:226 does have no production producer - both GuardianJudgeInput.facts sites (pi-agent.ts:3417-3421 and :3523-3527) set only mode and workspaceRoot - but that WEAKENS the finding: describeFacts (:322-328) gates the '(PROTECTED/default branch)' note on facts.gitBranch, which is also never set, so the note is never rendered in production and the judge's prompt never asserts a protected branch at all. Only the tests set either field.
correctedState: No divergence as stated. Nessy never implemented the 'Default / protected branches' context slot that v2.1.211 removed; the autoMode keys we parse are environment/hard_deny/soft_deny/allow only (managed-policy.ts:469). The sentence at guardian.ts:171 that keeps a default-branch git action 'high or critical' is Codex-derived policy text (openai/codex guardian policy.md, Apache-2.0), adopted deliberately and recorded in the file header and docs/architecture/guardian-command-judge.md, not a stale copy of a Claude default. Its effect on the case the finding names is the opposite of what was claimed: a routine user-requested push to main scores authorization 'high', clears rule :186 and the :173 deny rule, and returns no_objection, which turns a prompt Nessy would otherwise show into an allow. Only an unauthorized push (agent drift, authorization low/unknown) is denied. The protectedBranch fact is inert in both directions - never set, and therefore never rendered, since describeFacts gates the note on gitBranch, which is also never set. The residual and genuine observation - that our built-in rule text is Codex prose inside the guardian system prompt rather than Claude's four addressable default lists - is already recorded as f121.
